correctness.rationale: Proposition 12.1 gives h^(0,1)=2, h^(1,0)=1 and h^(2,0)=0 for the rank-one square, while Lemma 11.12 gives b_1=2. The (1,0) class survives because d_1 from constants is zero, its d_1 target is the zero group E_1^(2,0), and all later incoming/outgoing bidegrees are impossible. Thus E_infinity^(1,0) has dimension one, forcing E_infinity^(0,1) to have dimension one. The only differential capable of reducing E_1^(0,1) is d_1 to (1,1), since d_2 targets E_2^(2,0)=0 and later targets have negative q. Therefore its kernel is one-dimensional and its rank is exactly one. The punctured fibers have zero rank because the source proves E_1-degeneration there.
